title: Record that the helper-462 landing permutation needs 18 odd-denominator shears
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped proof. No new κ. The selected record stays `781451/250000000`.

For the landing permutation `P` of the open 25-shear helper-462 route, every swap-free word whose shear coefficients are rationals of odd denominator, and whose scale coefficients are units of that same ring, has at least 18 shears. Eighteen is achieved by 18 shears of coefficient `±1` and six scales by `-1`.

`P` is the permutation matrix of `σ = (4, 3, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2) = (0 4 7 2 5)(1 3 6)`. `det(P) = 1`. The seven-shear cleanup of PR #7012 sends the pinned matcher to `P`, but four of its scales are halves, so the cleanup is outside this coefficient class.

Over `F2`, every CNOT circuit for `P` has at least six links, six middles and six cuts, and those classes are disjoint, so the CNOT length is at least 18. The reverse of the six content exchanges is an 18-gate circuit with split `6/6/6`. Odd-denominator letters reduce modulo 2 to CNOTs or to the identity, so a word in this class needs at least 18 shears. The argument is written out in `research/helper462-landing-shear-floor/PROOF.md`.

This settles the proposed first step inside that coefficient class: there is no odd-denominator factorization of `P` into fewer than 18 shears. Concatenating the seven cleanup shears with any such landing factor, without cancelling a letter at the junction, has at least 25 shear letters. Twenty-five is not claimed to be minimal. Words with `2` in a denominator, other routes, and cross-junction cancellation remain open. This is not a supplier admission.

## Task and overlap

Base commit: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. Priority revision 8.

Card `supplier-boundary-audit`. Scope status: **refined**. The card's supplier-admission experiment is not this task. The work answers the first step of Discussion #1166 comment [19507690](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19507690) and of open PR #7012's first open question: factor the landing permutation in fewer than 18 shears. Question 2 of #7012, the unrestricted shear length of `P`, stays open outside the odd-denominator class.

Nearest work:

- Open PR #7012 records the 25-shear two-scale word and does not claim that 25 is minimal. This package does not re-record that word. It proves the landing factor cannot be shortened below 18 shears for odd-denominator coefficients.
- Merged PR #6954 is the one-scale 53-shear word. Merged PR #6947 is the seven-scale 27-shear route. The 29-shear one-scale schedule is a different lane.
- A local overlap search of package notes at this base, and a title search of open upstream PRs, did not find another proof of this landing-length statement. The search is not a novelty certificate.

Fork draft: https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/pull/221, head `e1378eac4f2b277a39112807ffc018bfd1c51bde`, based on the pinned upstream commit so the fork diff is this package only.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/helper462-landing-shear-floor/verify.py
python3.12 -O -B research/helper462-landing-shear-floor/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/helper462-landing-shear-floor
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/helper462-landing-shear-floor --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Observed: `PASS_HELPER462_LANDING_ODD_DENOMINATOR_SHEARS` with `shears=18`, `link=6 middle=6 cut=6`, `minimum_25_claimed=0`; `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with `outcome=partial`; `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at `e1378eac4f2b277a39112807ffc018bfd1c51bde`.

The verifier checks the pinned matcher, `det(S) = -16`, the cleanup landing, the explicit word, deletion of each of the 18 CNOTs, doubling each odd shear, the 16-row river-parity table, and the `6/6/6` split. It also checks the one-step predicates on all 1,008 CNOTs in `GL(3, F2)`. That census is a control on the predicates. The proof for `n = 8` is `PROOF.md`, not the census. No Lean, Docker, or selected cold replay was run. No exhaustive search over dyadic coefficients was run.

## Credit

Matcher and published elimination: Chris R / Clear1nsight, PR #4957, `research/bit-completed-backend-api`, using ai-nanachi #4760/#4814. The landing matrix, seven-shear cleanup and six content exchanges: open PR #7012. The link/middle/cut decomposition follows the shape of CNOT-length arguments for permutations; the counting used here is written out in the package and is not imported as a black box.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can a shear coefficient with 2 in its denominator factor this landing permutation in fewer than 18 shears? The mod-2 reduction does not apply. First step: one explicit shorter word, or a 2-adic obstruction. An incomplete search is not a minimality proof.
2. Can commutation or a Steinberg rewrite across the cleanup/landing junction delete one shear from the concatenated 25-letter word? The cleanup uses scales by `1/2`, so the odd-denominator theorem does not cover the product.
3. Is there a zero-swap word for this matcher, with at least two scales and fewer than 25 shears, that does not factor through this landing permutation?

## Workflow feedback (optional)

Keeping the 25-shear witness in #7012 and the landing-length proof in a separate package made the coefficient hypothesis explicit. The odd-denominator reduction is easy to over-read as a proof that 25 is minimal; the open questions are there to prevent that reading.
